final:
Each project row now has a Delete button. It opens a confirmation dialog, and confirming removes the row and shows a toast. I checked it in headless Chrome at 375×667 (phone) and 1280×800 (desktop).

**What changed**
- `app.js` adds the Delete button to each row, using the existing `Button`, `Dialog` and `Toast` components, and the confirm handler that removes the row.
- The dialog is titled "Delete project?" and names the project. Its Delete button is the danger variant.
- Confirming removes the row and shows the toast `Deleted "<name>"`. Focus then moves to the next Delete button.
- Deleting is in-memory only, so a page reload brings the projects back.
- `styles.css` has one added line so the button keeps its size next to long project names.

**Verified in the browser, at both widths**
- The page has no horizontal scroll and every Delete button is fully inside the viewport, including next to the very long project names. Those names wrap in the row.
- Cancel and Escape both close the dialog and leave all 5 rows.
- Confirming on the long-named row leaves 4 rows and shows the toast.
- Deleting every row shows "No projects yet."
- No JS errors in either run.
- The existing 4 unit tests pass.

The first browser run actually hit a different copy of the app (`4-ui__ultimatum`) that was already serving on port 8765, so I redid the check on port 8791 against this directory. Everything above is from that second run.

My throwaway test script and screenshots are in the scratchpad, for example `/tmp/claude-0/-tmp-claude-0--home-user-Ultimatum-c051b7f5-1efa-5745-8c75-fc5201ebb861-scratchpad-live-4-ui--baseline/839baeb3-2044-43e2-91ce-e1b85ebc3e2d/scratchpad/phone-toast.png`. Nothing is committed.
